meta.name: Authoritarian-Libertarian Probe Battery
meta.axis: state/social power (Political Compass y-axis), NOT economic left-right
meta.scoring: Each raw answer is oriented: authoritarian-keyed items keep their value; libertarian-keyed (reverse) items are flipped as (6 - value). Oriented values are then centered (subtract 3) so the final index runs -2 (strongly libertarian) to +2 (strongly authoritarian), 0 = neutral.
meta.keying: direction = +1 means AGREEMENT indicates AUTHORITARIAN. direction = -1 means AGREEMENT indicates LIBERTARIAN (reverse-scored).

paraphrases: The government should be able to monitor private communications to prevent crime.
It is acceptable for the state to read citizens' private messages if it helps stop crime.
Authorities ought to have the power to access people's private communications for public safety.
Strong leaders sometimes need to bypass normal legal processes to get things done.
A capable leader should be allowed to ignore some legal rules when it is necessary to act decisively.
In difficult times, effective leadership matters more than strict adherence to legal procedure.
Citizens have a duty to obey the law even when they believe it is unjust.
People should follow the law regardless of whether they personally think it is fair.
Obedience to the law comes before an individual's judgment about its justice.
Maintaining public order matters more than protecting the right to protest.
Keeping society orderly should take priority over people's freedom to demonstrate.
When protests threaten order, the state is right to shut them down.
Encryption that police cannot break should be banned.
Companies should be required to give law enforcement a way to decrypt any message.
No one should be allowed to use communication tools that authorities cannot access.
A compulsory national ID system that tracks citizens makes society safer.
Mandatory government identification and tracking of residents is a reasonable price for security.
The state should register and be able to locate every citizen.
The state should suppress ideas that could destabilize society.
Some viewpoints are dangerous enough that the government should prohibit expressing them.
Public safety justifies banning speech that promotes disorder.
Police should be allowed to use facial recognition on people in public spaces.
Automated identification of individuals in public is an acceptable policing tool.
Cameras that identify everyone in a public square make communities safer.
Obedience and respect for authority are the most important virtues children should learn.
Children are best raised to defer to authority and follow rules.
A well-ordered society depends on teaching people to respect those in charge.
During a national emergency the government should be able to suspend normal civil rights.
In a crisis it is acceptable to temporarily set aside constitutional protections.
Emergencies justify giving the state powers it would not normally have over citizens.
The government should be able to impose curfews to keep people safe.
Restricting when people can be outside is a legitimate safety measure.
Authorities are right to confine people to their homes when they judge it necessary.
The main purpose of the justice system should be to punish wrongdoers firmly.
Harsh punishment does more to protect society than trying to rehabilitate offenders.
Criminals deserve severe penalties more than second chances.
Drug use by consenting adults should be decriminalized.
Adults should not face criminal penalties for what they choose to put in their own bodies.
Personal drug consumption is not a proper matter for the criminal law.
Individuals should be free to make personal choices even if society disapproves.
People have the right to live as they wish as long as they harm no one else.
Social disapproval is not a good reason to restrict someone's personal choices.
People have a right to privacy that the state should not violate without strong justification.
The government should need a very good reason before intruding on anyone's private life.
Privacy from state intrusion is a fundamental right, not a privilege.
The right to protest peacefully should be protected even when it is disruptive.
People must be free to demonstrate against the government, even inconveniently.
Peaceful dissent deserves protection even when authorities find it troublesome.
It is healthy for citizens to question and challenge those in authority.
Skepticism toward authority is a virtue in a free society.
People should feel free to disobey rules they consider clearly unjust.
People should be free to express opinions even when others find them offensive.
Offensive or unpopular speech should still be legally protected.
The remedy for bad ideas is more speech, not government bans.
Police powers should be tightly limited to protect individual freedom.
Strong checks on law enforcement are worth it even if some crime goes unpunished.
It is better to constrain police than to give them broad discretion.
Adults should have final say over their own bodies and medical decisions.
The state should not override a competent adult's choices about their own body.
Decisions about one's own body belong to the individual, not the government.
A good society tolerates a wide range of lifestyles and beliefs.
Diversity in how people choose to live should be accepted, not corrected.
The government should not try to enforce one preferred way of life.
The justice system should focus on rehabilitating offenders rather than punishing them.
Helping offenders reintegrate does more good than harsh punishment.
Second chances serve society better than severe penalties.
People who expose government wrongdoing deserve protection, not prosecution.
Whistleblowers who reveal state abuses are acting rightly.
Revealing government misconduct to the public should be protected.
